The LLM must run inside SQL Server via ML Services
The API tier and the LLM are the same process
Vector search and full-text search use separate databases

The embedding API call
Hybrid retrieval in SQL Server
The LLM call, which is 80%+ of total latency

questions.explain: The recommended progression is containers for dev, Azure SQL serverless for staging/early production, then Hyperscale/Managed Instance/self-hosted — with promotion being a connection-string change since the T-SQL is identical.
options: Rewrite the application for each environment
Containers for local dev → Azure SQL serverless → Hyperscale/Managed Instance/self-hosted, promoted by connection-string change
Start on Azure SQL Hyperscale and never move
On-prem only, because VECTOR is not in Azure SQL

questions.explain: Embeddings are deterministic per model, so caching text→vector by SHA2_256(model + text) never goes stale — the cheapest latency win in the stack.
options: The completion cache, because LLM calls are cheapest
The retrieval cache, because corpus changes are rare
The embedding cache — the text→vector mapping is deterministic per model and never stale
None; caching AI outputs is unsafe
questions.q: Which of the three cacheable surfaces is correctness-safe and called the cheapest latency win?

questions.explain: The unifying principle: own durable assets (vectors, history, feedback, audit trails live in your SQL Server) and rent fungible compute (model inference, embedding API calls).
options: Own durable assets (vectors, history, audit trails); rent fungible compute (model inference, embedding calls)
Buy everything as managed services
Self-host the LLM and rent the database
Own the compute and rent the data storage
